assessment: The incumbent supplies embedded-caption previews and accessible history on existing infrastructure. It reached the intended preview within 15 minutes in 20/30 sessions. H1-O7 limits a general rendering-failure account: all nine single-correction sessions took five to 11 minutes without reported uncertainty. Multiple saves, out-of-order completion and inconsistent mapping records make version identification a plausible contributor, but do not establish its cause or explain all ten slow sessions. The sampled 49 processing hours do not establish festival capacity. These are stipulated synthetic observations.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: a durable preview identity binding an immutable caption snapshot and video hash, displayed when requesting and downloading, would reduce unintended version selection. Validate the worker inputs against that identity before exposing the artifact.
openings.delta: Replace inference from filenames and completion sequence with one inspectable source pair; retain delivered artifacts and their original caption snapshots.
openings.prediction: With deliberately reversed completion order, editors identify their requested pair correctly; any worker-input mismatch is detected before download. Persistent mistakes despite correct binding would weaken the selection explanation.
openings.probe: In private staging, use demonstration footage and two editors to compare current history with a minimal identity display under reversed completion. Record requested, consumed and downloaded hashes plus identification time. Check that the last delivered wording remains retrievable.
assumptions: Snapshot storage and input verification fit the four engineer-days and existing accounts.
Editors can recognize intended pairs from the displayed identity; installation output stays unchanged.

openings.claim: Do missed deadlines primarily reflect unavailable final-edit artifacts or difficulty identifying and reviewing artifacts already available?
openings.delta: Separate artifact readiness from editor completion before choosing whether to alter render scheduling.
openings.prediction: A scheduling explanation predicts most excess time precedes verified final-pair availability; an identification/review explanation predicts substantial elapsed time afterward.
openings.probe: Align render events with final-edit, verified-pair availability, selection and review timestamps in staged repeated-save and single-correction tasks; record waiting and active work separately within the editor-day.
assumptions: A small staged sample can distinguish large timing differences; it cannot establish the 30-session success target or festival demand.
